activation_evidence_requirements: Downstream contract patch merged and versioned.
Benchmark artifact proves the chosen tier is justified.
Runtime harness covers telemetry and error-correlation signals.
ERR-1 registration or explicit error-mapping approval exists.
Kill switch, rollout owner, and fallback mode are declared.

establishes: Native acceleration is an implementation boundary, never a sovereignty transfer.
Any native path that cannot prove scheduler safety, deterministic behavior, and fail-closed semantics MUST leave the BEAM boundary.

capability_adoption_matrix.notes: Best initial adoption target for offline scanner and signed artifact verification; TKT-1 eligibility is limited to TKT-CRED-V1 credential-envelope verification and native result remains subordinate until accepted by the owning contract.
capability_adoption_matrix.tkt_scope: TKT-CRED-V1 public-key signature verification only; no admission, issuance, payment, inventory, transfer, or revocation authority.

capability_adoption_matrix.notes: Suitable for bounded verification primitives only; TKT-1 eligibility is limited to constant-time credential signature/hash/fingerprint checks; IAM adoption does not authorize native password KDF work without amendment.
capability_adoption_matrix.tkt_scope: TKT-CRED-V1 signature, hash, and fingerprint comparison only.

capability_adoption_matrix.android_edge_scope: Only for adopted TKT-CRED-V1 edge verification canonicalization; ORD-1, PRICE-1, and LOCKS-1 acceptance remains backend-owned unless their contracts separately adopt edge use.
capability_adoption_matrix.notes: All adoption paths MUST preserve raw 16-byte UUID ordering and keep the owning contract authoritative for acceptance and tie-break semantics; TKT-1 may adopt this for credential payload preimage/fingerprint work.
capability_adoption_matrix.tkt_scope: TKT-CRED-V1 JCS/canonical preimage and payload_fingerprint_sha256 only.

capability_adoption_matrix.notes: Useful only where benchmark evidence justifies native acceleration; pricing-rule authority remains in PRICE-1.
Parse success never implies business acceptance; domain validation and policy remain in the owning contract. TKT-1 eligibility is limited to QR/wallet credential envelope parsing.
capability_adoption_matrix.tkt_scope: TKT-CRED-V1 QR/wallet envelope parse only; parse success is not scan acceptance.

capability_adoption_matrix.notes: Authentication KDF and broader crypto-worker authority require a separate constitutional amendment before activation.
Private-key signing remains forbidden inside the native boundary unless separately amended with vault/HSM review.

capability_adoption_matrix_rules.notes: Capability matrix entries are not descriptive only; they are release-governance fields that prevent accidental native sprawl.
capability_adoption_matrix_rules.tkt_candidate_scope_rule: TKT-1 candidate ownership is limited to credential-envelope computation. It SHALL NOT transfer admission, issuance, payment, inventory, transfer, refund, or revocation authority to native code.

capability_budget_binding.notes: RUST-1 defines hard ceilings only; every adopted capability MUST carry a tighter owner-specific budget in the adopting contract.

allowed.authority_limit: Verification result is advisory until accepted by the owning core contract and domain action.
allowed.description: Verify signed offline scanner payloads or signed ticket credential artifacts using public keys only.

allowed.authority_limit: MUST NOT mint business authority on its own; caller remains responsible for policy and state checks.
allowed.description: Perform constant-time equality checks, HMAC verification, or signature verification using approved algorithms and pinned libraries.

allowed.authority_limit: MUST preserve suite ordering rules, including raw 16-byte UUID sorting when UUID lists participate.
allowed.description: Build canonical byte preimages and compute hashes or MAC inputs for signed artifacts, deterministic proofs, and adopted ticket credential fingerprints.

allowed.authority_limit: Caller MUST validate resulting state transitions in the core domain.
allowed.description: Perform bounded deterministic math that is expensive enough to justify native acceleration but does not own business truth.

allowed.authority_limit: Parse success MUST NOT imply business acceptance; domain validation remains mandatory.
allowed.description: Parse hostile or highly structured binary payloads, including adopted ticket credential envelopes, into bounded, validated, fixed-shape values.

requires_separate_amendment.reason: Authentication KDF policy is broader than the initial ticketing-native boundary and requires explicit amendment before activation.
Any signing operation with authoritative private keys requires separate constitutional review, HSM/vault integration review, and explicit approval.

change_log: v1.4.0 adds TKT-1 as an eligible downstream owner for ticket credential envelope parse, canonicalization, fingerprinting, and public-key verification only.

v1.4.0 adds an explicit TKT native credential boundary: native outputs are fixed-shape verification classifications and MUST NOT imply admission, payment validity, inventory validity, transfer approval, revocation authority, or issuance authority.
v1.4.0 allows Android-edge canonicalization only for adopted TKT-CRED-V1 verification paths and keeps owning contracts authoritative for acceptance.
v1.3.0 clarifies capability-authority terminology by replacing ambiguous matrix language with explicit owning-contract authority and native non-authority fields.
v1.3.0 tightens selected capability-to-tier combinations, expands JNI and Android packaging discipline, and adds release-manifest ABI governance.
v1.3.0 adds verification keyset anti-rollback, signed remote update, provenance, and emergency revocation requirements for offline trust.

v1.3.0 expands runtime activation blockers, repo-lint hooks, native error codes, loader semantics, and rollout/testing requirements so activation is blocked by missing operational proof, not just missing text.
v1.2.0 converts native capability classes from implicit approval into explicit eligibility only; downstream owner contracts MUST adopt and budget a capability before it may be enabled.
v1.2.0 adds capability adoption matrix, ERR-1 registration discipline, and downstream budget binding so Rust remains an execution boundary rather than a stealth authority transfer.
v1.2.0 adds governance-floor dependencies for LINT-0 and GOV-0 to align repo-level native-boundary lint and waiver controls with the contract.

v1.1.0 hardening pass expands native-state bans, loader/fallback semantics, Android/JNI governance, verification keyset lifecycle, native-specific error surfaces, repo lint hooks, and runtime-harness declarations.
v1.1.0 narrows initial native allowlist by moving password KDF work out of default allowed scope and into a separate-amendment track.
v1.1.0 adds bounded input/output and parser/memory rules plus fuzz/property test requirements for hostile-parser surfaces.
v1.0.0 established the initial legislative boundary for native compute, Rustler, and external native worker boundaries under CS-0@3.0.0.

dependencies.reason: CS-0 defines the schema families and artifact contracts this bundle MUST satisfy.
BP-0 defines the canonical three-artifact bundle blueprint and gate discipline.
V42-0 is the constitutional source of truth for money, inventory, order snapshot, tenancy, and observability invariants that native code MUST NOT weaken.
Native acceleration MUST NOT bypass tenant isolation, org_id propagation, or transaction-local RLS discipline.
Order finalization and immutable price-capture authority remain in core order workflows, not in native code.
Native code MAY verify signed pricing artifacts but MUST NOT become pricing-rule or quote authority.
Seat holds, allocation truth, and first-commit-wins conflict arbitration remain authoritative in the seating contract.
Ledger posting, reversals, and financial immutability remain authoritative in finance workflows, not native code.
Native failures MUST map into canonical error envelopes and fail-closed semantics.
Native capabilities MUST be observable with kill-switches, latency histograms, fallback metrics, and incident visibility.
Native work MUST respect queue capacity and MUST NOT create unbounded backpressure inside the BEAM.
Native acceleration is allowed only when benchmarked against explicit performance budgets and latency envelopes.
Any native helper that participates in hash/signature preimages or contention-sensitive computation MUST preserve deterministic lock and ordering rules; it MUST NOT invent alternate arbitration.
Authentication, authorization, step-up, and privileged action control remain in governed identity flows, not native code.
RUST-1 gates MUST remain deterministic, machine-checkable where possible, and explicit about any runtime declarations.
Native-boundary anti-patterns, waivers, and repo scanning discipline MUST be enforced through governed lint rules rather than convention.
Native-boundary exceptions and waivers MUST remain compatible with suite governance review discipline.

economic_defense_policy.governance_scope_note: RUST-1 governs only the native-boundary constraints for adaptive friction; broader anti-abuse and economic-defense policy belongs in a dedicated contract.

key_compromise_response: Require resync before further offline trust where policy demands

err1_integration_requirements.notes: RUST-1 may describe local native error codes, but downstream contracts MUST NOT rely on ERR-1-native subcodes until ERR-1 registry membership exists.

allowed_only_when: The work is CPU-bound and bounded.
Benchmark evidence proves the capability materially benefits the platform or the edge verifier.
The call remains kill-switchable and observable.
The work cannot be cleanly split into smaller scheduler-safe chunks without destroying correctness or practicality.
DirtyCpu usage is explicitly justified in benchmark evidence rather than used as a default escape hatch.

required_when: The work is blocking, unbounded, or operationally risky inside the VM.
The work requires network, filesystem, HSM, large memory spikes, or third-party foreign runtimes.
transport_requirements: Authenticated local IPC or controlled network boundary

allowed_only_when: The function is demonstrably scheduler-safe under hot-path load.
The work is small enough that NIF overhead does not dominate.
A pure Elixir or existing OTP primitive is not already sufficient.

boot_may_continue_when_native_missing_on: The capability is feature-flagged off or optional.
A governed fallback path exists and is selected.
The missing native binary does not weaken a security-critical control.
boot_must_fail_when: A configured security-critical native capability has no governed fallback.
Required verification behavior would be silently bypassed.
ABI mismatch or native load failure would leave the platform in an ambiguous mixed-authority state.

RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-001.text: Native code MUST NOT become the authoritative source of truth for tenant authorization, inventory truth, pricing authority, order finalization, refund approval, payout eligibility, ledger posting, or admission truth.
RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-001.why: These capabilities are constitutional invariants owned by governed core contracts.

RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-002.text: Any Rustler NIF that cannot prove scheduler-safe bounded execution on the selected tier MUST be moved to an external worker boundary.
RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-002.why: The BEAM must remain responsive under attack and under load.

RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-003.text: Native code MUST NOT perform direct Repo access, Ash action invocation, or provider-side orchestration.
RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-003.why: Bypassing governed Elixir boundaries would destroy auditability and policy guarantees.

RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-004.text: Edge and scanner native code MAY verify only with public keys; private signing keys and master signing keys MUST remain backend-vault-only.
RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-004.why: Occasionally connected devices must verify, not sign.

RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-005.text: Whenever UUID lists participate in native hashing, signing, or apportionment tie-break logic, the implementation MUST normalize to raw 16-byte form and sort by unsigned lexicographic byte order ascending; string sorting is forbidden.
RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-005.why: Crypto and tie-break determinism must match the platform constitution exactly.

RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-006.text: Proof-of-work MAY be used only as adaptive friction after primary controls are in place and risk scoring has escalated; it MUST NOT become the default for good-standing authenticated user flows.
RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-006.why: Security cost-shifting must not become self-inflicted UX damage.

RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-007.text: Native capability changes MUST ship with benchmark evidence, threat model, owner assignment, feature flag, and kill switch.
RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-007.why: Native acceleration without rollback and evidence is uncontrolled blast radius.

RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-008.text: Mutable global native state, request-derived runtime caches, shared verifier pools, and static mut patterns are forbidden in v1 native boundaries.
RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-008.why: Native acceleration must remain stateless and must not create cross-request or cross-tenant ambiguity.

RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-009.text: Security-critical native capability load failure MUST fail closed or fail boot; it MUST NOT silently degrade into bypassed verification.
RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-009.why: Missing native binaries cannot be allowed to erase security controls through accidental fallback.

RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-010.text: Android and scanner-native integrations MUST use a minimal governed JNI bridge and MUST NOT embed business workflow logic, network orchestration, or master signing authority.
RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-010.why: Edge-native code is for bounded verification and parsing, not for growing a second application core.

RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-011.text: Verification keysets used by the edge MUST be versioned, kid-addressable, time-bounded, and revocation-aware; stale keysets MUST warn and then fail closed on the configured schedule.
RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-011.why: Offline verification only remains defensible when key lifecycle is explicit and governed.

RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-012.text: Hostile parser, canonicalization, and verification surfaces MUST ship with fuzzing, property tests, golden vectors, and runtime telemetry assertions before enablement.
RUST-1-INV-BOUNDARY-012.why: Static document freezes alone do not prove native behavior under hostile input or degraded rollout.

foundation_refs.reason: RUST-1 exists to preserve V42 constitutional invariants while allowing bounded native acceleration.

supersedes.reason: Adds TKT-1 ticket credential envelope eligibility while preserving native non-authority rules.
Hardens the native boundary by requiring explicit downstream adoption, ERR-1 registration discipline, and downstream budget binding before enablement.
Supersedes the initial legislative boundary with tighter downstream adoption and governance controls.

native_state_rules.exception_rule: Any mutable native state requires explicit contract amendment, threat model update, and new gates; v1 forbids it.

observability_requirements.incident_rule: Any native path that materially affects security verification and begins failing MUST enter visible incident handling; it MUST NOT auto-bypass verification.

purpose_and_boundaries.contract_role: Law for native compute boundaries, Rustler usage, and external native worker isolation inside Ticketing.
explicit_non_goals: Replacing Ash policies with native code
Moving core order, seating, finance, or tenancy orchestration into Rust
Using obscurity alone as a security control
governed_surfaces: Rustler NIF entrypoints called from Ticketing Elixir code
External native workers or Ports used for isolated long-running compute
Deterministic cryptographic verification and constant-time comparison helpers
Deterministic canonicalization, hashing, and bounded math helpers
Hostile binary parsing and normalization helpers
Android JNI bridge layer and scanner-native packaging boundary
purpose_and_boundaries.native_truth_rule: Native code MAY accelerate and verify; it MUST NOT become authoritative for tenant authorization, policy evaluation, inventory truth, price authority, order finalization, ledger posting, refund approval, payout eligibility, or admission truth.

blueprint_refs.reason: RUST-1 bundle structure, naming, and gate discipline derive from BP-0.

external_normative_refs: Erlang/OTP erl_nif guidance for scheduler-safe execution, splitting, dirty NIF discipline, and fallback stubs
Rustler scheduler flags and panic-handling guidance

Android Keystore guidance for non-exportable device key material and scoped device trust

summary: Governs bounded Rust/Rustler/JNI native execution for Ticketing, including explicit TKT-1 credential-envelope eligibility, while preserving V42 authority in owning contracts. Native code MAY parse, canonicalize, and verify credential artifacts only after downstream adoption; it MUST NOT own business authority.

supply_chain_policy.unsafe_rust_exception_rule: Two-person review, explicit justification, bounded scope, and security sign-off required.

title: RUST-1 Native Compute, Rustler, JNI, and Ticket Credential Boundary Contract (Ticketing / Ash 3.x)

activation_preconditions: TKT-1 MUST explicitly adopt the exact capability IDs.
ERR-1 MUST register the mapped TKT_NATIVE/TKT_CREDENTIAL subcodes before suite lock.
OBS-1 MUST declare native TKT verification metrics and alerting.
PSC-1 MUST declare capability-specific latency and payload budgets.
Runtime harness MUST exercise success, malformed, invalid signature, unsupported kid, stale keyset, and budget-exceeded paths.
Feature flag and kill-switch MUST fail closed for security-critical edge verification.

owner_authority_rules.ORD-1: Order finalization and paid issuance trigger remains authoritative.
owner_authority_rules.PRICE-1: Price snapshot and price-line authority remains authoritative.
owner_authority_rules.SEAT-1: Inventory and seat allocation truth remains authoritative.
owner_authority_rules.TKT-1: Credential lifecycle and envelope law remains authoritative.

tkt_native_credential_boundary.scope: TKT-1 MAY adopt eligible native capabilities only for TKT-CRED-V1 QR/wallet credential envelope parsing, canonical preimage/fingerprint generation, constant-time comparison, and public-key verification.
